title: Classify 64 exchanged P104 eight-root complements for the f22 loose row
body:
Classifies all 64 one-root exchanges. The 40 nonunit complements miss 52 target ports while the loose row can cover four. The 24 unit complements each have sharp attained price 63.

## Scope and source

Builds on the fixed E8 complement and order-four f22 loose row of #7902. DreamingOfClouds’ Q=0 and thin toolkit extension is #7869 at `06c207a9feb3994a4b987dc3010657b6e85b7956`. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-decoder-exchanged-tight-bases/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. `python3 -B verify.py` regenerated the exact result and all integer witnesses. `python3 -B crosscheck.py` independently checked the 4^8 fibres and plane census. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Analyze two-root exchanges with the same witnesses and price convention. Arbitrary complements and Wall56 remain open.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
